landing.eyebrow: Clean fields · Clearer air · Stronger Punjab
landing.heroBody: A promised date for the Super Seeder, so no farmer has to burn paddy stubble while waiting for it.
landing.farmerRoleBody: Sees one date in large type: firm for the next two days, a window further out that narrows to a firm date. If it moves, the reason is right there.
landing.operatorRoleBody: Opens tomorrow's plan: each machine's stops in order, who is at burn risk, one button to approve. Marks a machine as broken and watches the plan re-form.
landing.how1Body: Constraint programming (OR-Tools CP-SAT) assigns fields to machines and days. Every promise is a hard constraint.
landing.how2Body: Tomorrow's route for each machine waits for one approval. Windows become firm dates only then.
landing.how3Body: Ask "why this date?" and Vaari re-runs the solver with your field one day earlier. What blocks it becomes the reason.
landing.fact1: Uncertainty over when a machine will arrive is a main reason farmers burn stubble.
landing.fact2: Each week of sowing delay past the optimum costs about 150 kg of wheat per acre.
landing.honestyTitle: What is real and what is simulated
landing.honestyBody: The farmers, fields, machines and breakdowns in this demo are simulated. Village names and locations come from OpenStreetMap. The sowing optimum (first fortnight of November) is from PAU. When fields become ready comes from NASA FIRMS fire detections around each village in the 2024 and 2025 seasons, moved 3 days earlier (an assumption). Satellites show heat, not intent, and miss some fires.
landing.fireMapPending: Not connected yet. It will show NASA FIRMS detections over Sangrur from the last 24 hours, as a lower bound: satellites pass once or twice a day and miss some fires.
landing.airBody: No fire lit while waiting for a machine
landing.problemTitle: Every autumn, Punjab's fields go up in smoke.
landing.problemBody: Once the paddy is cut, a farmer has a few weeks to sow wheat. A Super Seeder sows straight through the stubble, but a whole cluster of villages shares a handful of them. When nobody can say when the machine will come, a match is the fastest way to clear the field, and the smoke settles over the villages and the plains beyond.
landing.problemTurn: Farmers are not the problem. Waiting is. So Vaari takes the guesswork out of the wait.
landing.stat2Label: hotspot villages in eight districts had nearly two-thirds of them
landing.stat3Label: fire detections by two NASA satellites over our Sangrur area, Sept to Dec 2024
landing.stat4Label: of those detections (2024 and 2025) came in 1 to 15 November, the best fortnight to sow wheat
landing.chartBody: Fire detections per day over the Sangrur area in October and November, 2024 and 2025 seasons together. They peak in the very weeks wheat should be sown.
landing.chartLabel: Bar chart. {total} fire detections in the 2024 and 2025 seasons; the busiest day was {peakDate} with {peakCount}. {share}% came in 1 to 15 November.
landing.chartSource: NASA FIRMS, VIIRS on the Suomi NPP and NOAA-20 satellites; low-confidence detections left out, and a fire seen by both counts twice. Satellites pass once or twice a day and miss some fires, so these counts are a lower bound. They show heat, not who lit it.
landing.fixTitle: Replace the wait with a date.
landing.fixBody: Vaari plans every Super Seeder of a Custom Hiring Centre (a co-operative that rents out sowing machines) and gives each farmer a numbered token with a promised date. When a machine breaks, it re-plans without silently breaking a promise.
landing.closingTitle: Clean air starts with a date.
landing.closingBody: Walk through the simulated season as a farmer or as the operator. One click, no sign-up.
landing.footerPhotos: Photos on this page are AI-generated illustrations, not the demo's farmers or fields.
landing.footerCredits: Fire data: NASA FIRMS. Villages: © OpenStreetMap contributors. Sowing window and yield loss: PAU Package of Practices.

proof.title: Does a promised date actually help?
proof.body: Vaari against two ways CHCs work today, a phone queue (first come, first served) and nearest village next, on the same simulated seasons: real villages and real harvest timing from NASA FIRMS, simulated farmers, machines, breakdowns and rain.
proof.replayBody: Each dot is one farmer's field at its real village across Sangrur district, at the end of one simulated season: the median of all {runs}, typical rather than the best case. Squares are machine centres. Outlines: OpenStreetMap.
proof.mapLabel: {policy}: {onTime} fields sown by {date}, {late} sown after it, {burned} burned
proof.tableCaption: Median over {runs} simulated seasons, with the 10th to 90th percentile below each value.
proof.scenarioNote_base: Every centre's farmers and machines across the district, under the same weather. The phone queue is run the way CEEW finds most centres run it: a rental desk, with the machine back at the centre between farmers.
proof.metric_fieldsLate: Farmers not reached by their last waiting day
proof.metric_fieldsLatePct: Share of farmers not reached by their last waiting day
proof.metric_wheatLostKg: Wheat lost (150 kg per acre per week late, PAU)
proof.metric_incomePerMachineRupees: Income per machine at ₹{rent} an acre (CEEW)
proof.metric_worstDelayVsQueueDays: Worst delay for one farmer, compared with the phone queue
proof.breakEven: CEEW: a CHC breaks even at about {acres} acres per machine a season.
proof.sweepTitle: What if our assumptions are wrong?
proof.sweepBody: One machine centre ({centre}) replayed with one input changed, {runs} seasons per value. The line is the median; the band is the 10th to 90th percentile.
proof.assumptionsBody: Every input, labelled. Assumed values are our choice; real ranges come from the source named.
proof.in_harvestReadyDay: Harvest day: each village's real fire timing (NASA FIRMS 2024–2025)
proof.in_seasonWindow: Fields ready from day {first} to day {last} of the season (1 October is day 0)

proof.sweepTitle_daysSoonerWithoutDate: Farmers without a date give up sooner

proof.sweepNote_waitingLimitDays: Every farmer waits exactly this many days after harvest before burning. In the base season each farmer's patience is drawn between 3 and 10 days.
proof.sweepNote_daysSoonerWithoutDate: How much sooner a farmer with no promised date gives up and burns. No study measures it, so the headline assumes {base} days; here it runs 0 to 3.

proof.in_daysSoonerWithoutDate: {value, plural, =0 {A farmer with no date gives up no sooner than one holding a promise} one {A farmer with no date gives up # day sooner} other {A farmer with no date gives up # days sooner}}

privacy.metaDescription: What Vaari keeps about farmers and helpers, why, who processes it, how long we keep it, and how to have it deleted.
privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: What Vaari keeps about you, why, and how to have it deleted.
privacy.whoBody: Vaari is a hackathon project. It plans Super Seeder visits so every farmer gets a promised date for sowing wheat. Write to us at <email>{address}</email>.
privacy.collectFarmersLead: About farmers (a village helper books for them, with their consent):
privacy.collectFarmerWaitingLimit: How many days you can wait for the machine
privacy.collectFarmerWhatsapp: WhatsApp messages and voice notes sent to the Vaari number
privacy.collectStaffGoogle: Name and email from Google sign-in
privacy.whyPurpose: Only to plan machine visits and tell farmers their date.
privacy.processorsLead: Two companies handle this data for us:
privacy.processorsAws: Amazon Web Services (AWS): hosts Vaari, stores the data, turns voice notes into text, and uses AI to word explanations. The planner sets every date, not the AI.
privacy.accessHelpers: Village helpers: only the fields they booked.
privacy.accessOperators: Operators: only their own machine centre.
privacy.accessOfficers: Agriculture officers: totals only, never phone numbers.
privacy.retentionBookings: Booking data: until the end of the season.
privacy.retentionVoice: Voice notes: deleted once turned into text, and always within 30 days.
privacy.deletionWhatToSay: Tell us the phone number your fields were booked with. Staff: the email you sign in with.
privacy.deletionWhatsappSoon: Asking on WhatsApp is not available yet. Please use email.

machines.loanNote: Away on a loan: it comes back when the district officer ends the loan.
machines.draftTitle: A re-plan is waiting for you
machines.draftBody: Check what changes for farmers, then approve. Nothing changes for them until you do.
machines.conflict: That cannot be done: a machine on loan stays until the district officer ends the loan, and a centre keeps at least one machine of its own.
machines.footnote: Adding or removing a machine makes a new plan for you to check. Loans between centres are arranged by the district officer. Speeds start from a sourced range (5.3 to 12 acres a day) and are learned from work logs.
machines.addBody: A machine you bought or rented in. It works from tomorrow, and a new plan gives it fields for you to check.
machines.removeBody: A new plan shares its fields among your other machines. Promises stay: if one cannot hold, the plan tells you before you approve.

fleet.byCentre: By centre, most load per machine first
fleet.footnote: Acres booked per machine: fields booked with the centre so far this season, sown or waiting, for each machine it owns. CEEW puts a Super Seeder's break-even at about 105 acres a season, so mid-season most centres are still below it.

day.title: Today, {date}
day.recordBody: {count, plural, one {# field was} other {# fields were}} planned today. Untick any that were not sown, then save.
day.approveFirst: Approve tomorrow's plan to start tomorrow.
day.recordHint: A sown field keeps its promise and teaches the machine's speed. A field not sown goes into tomorrow's plan.
day.blocked: Record today's work and approve tomorrow's plan first.
day.failed: That did not go through. Try again in a moment.
day.startBody: The season moves on one day for every centre. The machines follow the approved plan, and helpers and farmers see the new day.

changeBooking.title: Change this booking
changeBooking.body: Tell the centre what changed. The old date ends, and the next plan gives a new one.
changeBooking.harvestHint: The machine cannot come before the field is harvested.
changeBooking.cancelBody: For example the field was sown another way.
changeBooking.cancelSure: Cancel this booking for good? The centre gives the slot to another farmer, and this link stops working.
changeBooking.failed: That did not go through. Try again in a moment.
